items.title: feat(deploy): slice 3 — real systemd activation with health-check flip-back (#5766)
items.body: Closes the remaining acceptance of #5766 (deploy tool v1): slices 1–2 (PR #6231, PR #7692) shipped the registry, unit rendering, dry-run plans, generation log, and status/rollback logic; the non-dry-run paths refused explicitly. This slice implements real activation. **What changed** - `pkgs/deploy/deploy.py`: real (non-dry-run) `deploy` and `rollback` for the systemd class, in the design §4.1 plan order — install the generation into the per-service profile, write the unit, daemon-reload, restart only that unit, run the health check, flip back on any failure. - The profile is deploy-managed: the profile link points at a generation directory whose `current` symlink names the artifact (the rendered unit's `/current/` path resolves through it), so a flip is one atomic symlink repoint. Store-path artifacts are additionally registered with `nix-env --set` on a parallel `.nix-env-profile`. - Rollback repoints at the previous distinct generation and restarts — never a rebuild (§4.6). On health failure it flips back to the generation that was current. - Failed activations append a non-folding `deploy_failed`/`rollback_failed` generation-log entry, so the current/previous fold never mistakes a failure for an activation. - New `--unit-dir` / `--scope system|user` (user scope exists so the laptop E2E can deploy a harmless service without root). Launchd real activation still refuses explicitly — it cannot be exercised from the Linux fleet. - Tests: `test_deploy_slice3.py` (new, 7 tests, faked runner/prober asserting the §4.1 order, flip-back, rollback, and the recorded-not-raised flip-back-failure regression), wired into `lib/default.nix` checks as `deploy-slice3-tests`; the slice-2 refusal test updated to the new behavior. Slice-2 suite 21/21, slice-3 7/7, dupkeys/argv suites pass on the laptop. **Laptop E2E acceptance (2026-11-09T00:49Z, user scope, harmless `deploy-e2e` service, no nixos-rebuild / home-manager in the loop)** — full log on #5766 (comment 6729616258): 1. deploy v1 → generation 1 activated, serves; status current gen 1, health ok. 2. deploy v2 → generation 2, serves v2. 3. rollback → serves v1 again. 4. deploy broken generation → health check fails, auto-flips back to generation 3, serves v2, final status health ok. The first E2E run caught a real bug — a broken unit restart-loops into systemd's start limit, so flip-back now issues `reset-failed` before restarting and never raises (a flip-back failure is a recorded outcome, not a crash). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.body: ## Summary Slice 2 of issue #5766 (deploy tool v1), building on slice 1 (PR #6231, merged: `deployTargets` registry + `deploy list` + definition validation). Queue task 13021. What lands in `pkgs/deploy/deploy.py`: - **Systemd unit rendering** (`render_unit`) and a **launchd plist stub** (`render_plist`) from a registry definition. The rendered `ExecStart` / program path points at the service's per-service nix profile `current` link (`/nix/var/nix/profiles/per-service//current/`, design §4.1) — never at a bare store path — so a generation flip is a profile repoint and the rendered file is identical for every generation of the same definition. systemd argument/environment quoting escapes whitespace, quotes, backslashes, and doubles the `%`/`$` introducers. - **`deploy --dry-run`**: the ordered §4.1 activation plan (build → install next generation into the profile → write unit/plist → daemon-reload → restart only that unit → health check → flip back on failure → append to the generation log), with no side effects. - **Generation log** (design §4.6): append-only JSONL per target under the state dir (`--state-dir` / `$DEPLOY_STATE_DIR`), one record per activation event carrying generation id, source rev, artifact, timestamp, actor, action, result. Logs are never truncated (two generations always retained). - **`deploy status`**: folds the log into current/previous generations (a rollback event makes the generation it repointed to current) and reports the health verdict for the target's `healthCheck` URL, or that no check is defined. - **`rollback` command logic**: selects the previous *distinct* generation (repointing, never rebuilding) and is refused when fewer than two distinct generations were ever current. - Real activation — `nix-env` profile install, `systemctl` restart, health-check flip-back — is the next slice: the non-dry-run deploy/rollback paths say so explicitly and exit non-zero rather than pretending to have activated something. The remaining on-laptop E2E acceptance from issue #5766 also stays open there. ## Tests - New `pkgs/deploy/test_deploy_slice2.py` (21 tests, stdlib unittest): unit/plist rendering invariants, generation-log round-trip/fold/rollback-fold, plan ordering and flip-back step, rollback refusal cases, status formatting, and CLI subprocess cases (dry-run creates no state, real deploy refused, seeded-log status, unknown target). Oracle: design §4.1/§4.2/§4.6 + the issue text, named in the test module docstring. - New flake check `deploy-slice2-tests` in `lib/default.nix` next to `deploy-dupkeys-property`, running the new test file against `deploy.py` in CI. - Existing coverage re-verified locally on the laptop against the new `deploy.py`: `test_dupkeys_property.py` (300 cases, property holds), `deploy list` on a valid registry, malformed registry rejected with field-level errors, `status` on an empty log. Refs #5766 (issue stays open for the activation slice + E2E acceptance). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: design(release): release workflow for per-app version tags (#11177)
items.body:
Design record for #11177, the #5790 §5 remainder (its other area, the deploy-tool identity ledger #5766, is closed).

**Decides:**

- **Actor/trigger**: the deploy tool cuts the tags — a new `deploy release` verb in `pkgs/deploy/deploy.py`, invoked deliberately by an operator. CI never creates tags (it only builds from them); unaided manual `git tag` is not a release path. The owner's 2026-11-13 disabling of mcpx's automatic tag-push publishing is read as the standing preference for deliberate release acts.
- **Attestation**: "tested" = the main-gate verdict for the exact commit (the `main-broken.yml` watched set, judged by the existing `.github/scripts/release-gate.sh` rules) plus the app's own test workflow when it sits outside the watched set (fleet: `fleet-rust-tests` — the watched set has no fleet workflow; recorded in the design). Stored in the annotated tag message (`release-attestation:v1` block), mirrored in a deploy-ledger release log read by `deploy status`, and closed out by the artifact reporting the clean version.
- **Refusal (§3.9)**: lives in the deploy tool — deploy-time refusal of any release-claiming deploy without a verifiable attested tag at the artifact's commit, and release-time refusal on any failed precondition. Prerelease deploys from main are untouched and never promoted.
- **First tags**: explicit recorded decision (§7) — no hand-cut tags ahead of the tool; the first per-app tags wait for the follow-on implementation issue. `mcpx/v0.1.0` is grandfathered as that app's 0.1.0.

Docs only; `git diff --check` clean; no schedule created/changed/retired; no new dependencies. Refs #11177 (no closing keyword — the issue stays open until Felix's review/merge and the #5790 link).

### Tokio broadcast channel calls clone in parallel, but does not require `Sync`
[GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The broadcast channel internally calls `clone` on the stored value when receiving it, and only requires `T:Send`. This means that using the broadcast channel with values that are `Send` but not `Sync` can trigger unsoundness if the `clone` implementation makes use of the value being `!Sync`.

Thank you to Austin Bonander for finding and reporting this issue.
